question: Which submission pipeline supplies the raw data behind the diabetes medication adherence rate?
reference_answer: The measure is built from Prescription Drug Event (PDE) data submitted by drug plans to CMS Drug Data Processing Systems (DDPS) and accepted by the 2024 PDE submission deadline for annual Part D payment reconciliation, with dates of service from January 1, 2024-December 31, 2024.

question: What is the primary data source for the Breast Cancer Screening measure, and what data source category does it fall under?
reference_answer: The primary data source for Breast Cancer Screening is HEDIS, and its data source category is Health and Drug Plans.

question: Do stand-alone prescription drug plans have to report the colorectal cancer screening measure?
reference_answer: No. In the Colorectal Cancer Screening reporting requirements, PDP is marked "No" while 1876 Cost, CCP w/o SNP, CCP with SNP, CCP with Only I-SNP, MSA, and PFFS contracts are all marked "Yes".

question: Which CMS system do the complaint counts for the Part C complaints measure come out of?
reference_answer: Complaints about the Health Plan is drawn from the Complaints Tracking Module (CTM) in the Health Plan Management System (HPMS), based on the contract entry date; its data source category is CMS Administrative Data.

question: Where do the Annual Flu Vaccine numbers actually come from - claims data or something else?
reference_answer: Not claims - the measure comes from the CAHPS survey (data source category Survey of Enrollees), based on the survey question "Have you had a flu shot since July 1, 2024?".

question: Which database identifies the members who switched away from their plan for the disenrollment measure?
reference_answer: Members Choosing to Leave the Plan uses the Medicare Beneficiary Database Suite of Systems (MBDSS) as its primary data source; the data source category is CMS Administrative Data.

question: What data sources are used for the MPF Price Accuracy measure?
reference_answer: MPF Price Accuracy uses PDE data and MPF Pricing Files, with reference data sources including HPMS approved formulary extracts, the Formulary Reference File, RxNorm, FDA NSDE data, and data from First DataBank and Medi-span; the data source category is Data Collected by CMS Contractors.

question: Is an MSA contract on the hook for reporting the MTM CMR completion rate?
reference_answer: No. The MTM Program Completion Rate for CMR reporting requirements mark MSA as "No", while 1876 Cost, CCP w/o SNP, CCP with SNP, CCP with Only I-SNP, PDP, and PFFS contracts are marked "Yes".

question: How many diabetes medication fills — and how long a treatment period — put a Part D member into the diabetes adherence denominator?
reference_answer: The denominator requires continuously enrolled beneficiaries 18 years and older with at least two fills of diabetes medication(s) on unique dates of service during the measurement period, and a treatment period that is at least 91 days during the measurement year.

question: If a member's Part D coverage lapses mid-treatment, can they still qualify for the hypertension (RAS antagonist) adherence measure?
reference_answer: No — continuous enrollment (CE) means being continuously enrolled in a Medicare Part D contract during the treatment period with no enrollment gaps allowed during the treatment period.

question: What is the denominator for the Breast Cancer Screening measure in the 2026 Star Ratings Technical Notes?
reference_answer: Women MA enrollees 52 to 74 years of age as of December 31 of the measurement year; the numerator is those who had a mammogram to screen for breast cancer in the past two years.

question: Under the 2025 Star Ratings, which women were counted in the mammogram screening population?
reference_answer: For the 2025 Star Ratings the metric covers women MA enrollees 50 to 74 years of age as of December 31 of the measurement year who had a mammogram in the past two years.

question: An 86-year-old MA member has a hypertension diagnosis — does she fall inside the population measured for blood pressure control?
reference_answer: No. The Controlling Blood Pressure denominator covers MA members 18–85 years of age who had a diagnosis of hypertension (HTN), so an 86-year-old is outside the measured population.

question: At what age does someone start counting toward the colorectal cancer screening rate, and when do they age out?
reference_answer: The measure covers MA enrollees aged 50 to 75 as of December 31 of the measurement year, so members enter the denominator at age 50 and age out after 75.

question: Does the diabetes eye exam measure include people with type 1 diabetes, and what ages does it span?
reference_answer: Yes — the denominator is diabetic MA enrollees age 18-75 with diabetes (type 1 and type 2); the numerator is a retinal eye exam performed during the measurement year.

question: Whose lab results get looked at for the blood-sugar control (glycemic status) rating — which members make up that population?
reference_answer: The denominator is diabetic MA enrollees age 18-75; the numerator counts those whose most recent HbA1c level is greater than 9% or who were not tested during the measurement year, and the rate is reverse scored for public reporting.

question: Up to what age can a member with diabetes be counted in the kidney health evaluation measure?
reference_answer: The measure covers members 18–85 years of age with diabetes (type 1 and type 2) who received a kidney health evaluation — an eGFR and a uACR — during the measurement year.

question: Is there a minimum age for the hospital-stay population in the plan all-cause readmission rate?
reference_answer: Yes — the measure counts acute inpatient stays for members 18 years of age and older that were followed by an unplanned acute readmission for any diagnosis within 30 days.

question: What are the age criteria for males versus females in the Statin Therapy for Patients with Cardiovascular Disease denominator?
reference_answer: Males 21–75 years of age and females 40–75 years of age during the measurement year who were identified as having clinical atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD).

question: Who ends up in the statin-use-for-diabetes population, and is any break in enrollment tolerated?
reference_answer: Part D beneficiaries 40-75 years old who were dispensed at least two diabetes medication fills on unique dates of service, with an IPSD at least 90 days before the end of the measurement period; continuous enrollment permits one allowable gap in enrollment of up to one calendar month.

question: Does being on insulin change whether a beneficiary counts in the diabetes medication adherence denominator?
reference_answer: Yes. Beneficiaries with one or more prescriptions for insulin in the treatment period are excluded from the Medication Adherence for Diabetes Medications denominator, alongside beneficiaries in hospice and those with an ESRD diagnosis or dialysis coverage dates.

question: A 70-year-old member has been living long-term in a nursing facility all year - does she still count toward the breast cancer screening rate?
reference_answer: No. Medicare members 66 years of age and older by the end of the measurement period are excluded from Breast Cancer Screening if they were enrolled in an Institutional SNP (I-SNP) any time during the measurement year or were living long-term in an institution any time during the measurement year.

question: If a member starts receiving comfort-focused palliative care mid-year, does the Controlling Blood Pressure measure still include them?
reference_answer: No. Controlling Blood Pressure requires excluding members receiving palliative care any time during the measurement period, as well as members who had an encounter for palliative care any time during the measurement period (not including laboratory claims).

question: For colorectal cancer screening, is showing signs of frailty by itself enough to drop an older member from the measure?
reference_answer: No. Members 66 years of age and older by the end of the measurement period must meet BOTH the frailty and the advanced illness criteria to be excluded: at least two indications of frailty with different dates of service, plus advanced illness on at least two different dates of service or a dispensed dementia medication.

question: A member's only diabetes-related diagnosis was gestational diabetes during pregnancy - is she pulled out of the Diabetes Care Eye Exam measure?
reference_answer: Yes, that is a required exclusion: members who did not have a diagnosis of diabetes, in any setting, during the measurement year or the year prior, and who had a diagnosis of polycystic ovarian syndrome, gestational diabetes or steroid-induced diabetes in that same window, are excluded from the Eye Exam measure.

question: How does CMS spot the long-term institutionalized members it removes from the blood sugar control measure?
reference_answer: For Diabetes Care - Blood Sugar Controlled, Medicare members 66 years of age and older as of December 31 of the measurement year are excluded if living long-term in an institution any time during the measurement year, as identified by the LTI flag in the Monthly Membership Detail Data File (or if enrolled in an I-SNP).

question: Someone whose kidneys have already failed and who is on dialysis - do they factor into the kidney health evaluation rate for diabetes patients?
reference_answer: No. The Kidney Health Evaluation for Patients with Diabetes measure excludes members with evidence of ESRD or dialysis any time during the member's history on or prior to December 31 of the measurement year.

question: Which hospital stays never enter the Plan All-Cause Readmissions calculation at all?
reference_answer: Hospital stays are excluded when the member died during the stay, when there is a principal diagnosis of pregnancy on the discharge claim, or when there is a principal diagnosis of a condition originating in the perinatal period on the discharge claim; members in hospice or using hospice services any time during the measurement year are also excluded.

question: Which muscle problems keep a member out of the statin therapy measure for people with cardiovascular disease?
reference_answer: Members with myalgia, myositis, myopathy, or rhabdomyolysis during the measurement year are excluded from Statin Therapy for Patients with Cardiovascular Disease.

question: What are the required exclusions for the Transitions of Care measure?
reference_answer: Required exclusions are members in hospice or using hospice services any time during the measurement year and members who died any time during the measurement year; both the initial and readmission/direct transfer discharge are also excluded if the last discharge occurs after December 1 of the measurement year.

What share of days must be covered by fills for a member to count as adherent to their cholesterol (statin) medication?
reference_answer: A member counts in the numerator with a proportion of days covered (PDC) of 80 percent or higher for statin cholesterol medication(s) during the measurement period.

question: How few continuously enrolled members can a contract have before it drops out of the diabetes adherence measure entirely?
reference_answer: Contracts with 30 or fewer continuously enrolled beneficiaries (in the denominator) are excluded from the measure.

question: Below what blood pressure reading is a hypertensive member's BP considered under control for the CBP numerator?
reference_answer: Blood pressure is counted as adequately controlled when it is less than 140/90 mm Hg.

question: From what age can a colorectal screening member be dropped for living long-term in an institution or being in an I-SNP?
reference_answer: Medicare members 66 years of age and older by the end of the measurement period are excluded if they were enrolled in an Institutional SNP (I-SNP) or living long-term in an institution any time during the measurement period.

question: What is the 5-star cut point for Breast Cancer Screening in the 2026 Star Ratings?
reference_answer: A contract earns 5 stars with a rate greater than or equal to 84%; the 1-star band is a rate less than 58%.

question: Above what HbA1c value does a diabetic member count against the plan in the glycemic status measure — and what if no test was done?
reference_answer: The numerator counts members whose most recent HbA1c level is greater than 9%, or who were not tested during the measurement year; the measure is reverse scored for public reporting so higher scores are better.

question: Which enrollment-size and reliability thresholds exclude a contract from the Plan All-Cause Readmissions measure?
reference_answer: Contracts whose enrollment was at least 500 but less than 1,000 as of the July 2024 enrollment report and having measure score reliability less than 0.7 are excluded, and contracts whose enrollment was less than 500 are excluded; CMS also excluded contracts whose denominator was less than 150.

question: How much does the hypertension medication adherence measure weigh in the overall Star Rating, and what measure type is it?
reference_answer: Medication Adherence for Hypertension (RAS antagonists) carries a weighting value of 3 and is classified as an Intermediate Outcome Measure.

question: What is the data time frame for the Call Center - Foreign Language Interpreter and TTY Availability measures in the 2026 Star Ratings?
reference_answer: Both the Part C and Part D Call Center – Foreign Language Interpreter and TTY Availability measures use data from 02/2025 – 05/2025.

question: What measurement period does the Controlling Blood Pressure measure cover for the 2026 Star Ratings?
reference_answer: For the 2026 Star Ratings, Controlling Blood Pressure uses data from 01/01/2024 – 12/31/2024, i.e. the full 2024 calendar year.

question: When were the survey responses behind the annual flu shot measure actually gathered for the 2026 Star Ratings?
reference_answer: The Annual Flu Vaccine measure in the 2026 Star Ratings draws on data collected 03/2025 – 05/2025 (March through May 2025).

question: Is any data collection window attached to the Health Plan Quality Improvement measure in the 2026 Star Ratings?
reference_answer: No - the data time frame for Health Plan Quality Improvement is listed as "Not Applicable".

question: The 2026 Star Ratings score plans on whether members' physical activity gets monitored - over what stretch of 2024 were those data gathered?
reference_answer: Monitoring Physical Activity draws on data from 07/17/2024 – 11/01/2024, i.e. July 17 through November 1, 2024.

question: Does MPF Price Accuracy use a full calendar year of data in the 2026 Star Ratings, or something shorter?
reference_answer: Something shorter: MPF Price Accuracy covers 01/01/2024 – 09/30/2024, only the first nine months of 2024.

question: Did the window of service data behind Breast Cancer Screening move between the 2025 and 2026 Star Ratings?
reference_answer: Yes, it rolled forward one year: the 2025 Star Ratings use Breast Cancer Screening data from 01/01/2023 – 12/31/2023, while the 2026 Star Ratings use 01/01/2024 – 12/31/2024.

question: What score earned a plan 5 stars on the blood-sugar control measure in the 2025 Star Ratings, and where did that bar land for 2026?
reference_answer: In the 2025 Star Ratings, 5 stars on Diabetes Care - Blood Sugar Controlled required a score of at least 90% (">= 90 %"); for the 2026 Star Ratings the 5-star cut point rose to greater than or equal to 91%.

question: The blood-sugar control measure points to a different underlying HEDIS specification in the 2026 Star Ratings than it did in 2025 - what changed?
reference_answer: The underlying HEDIS measure was renamed: the 2025 Star Ratings reference "Hemoglobin A1c Control for Patients with Diabetes (HBD)", while the 2026 Star Ratings reference "Glycemic Status Assessment for Patients With Diabetes (GSD)" - HbA1c poor control (greater than 9.0%).

question: How did CMS change the weighting of the patient experience, complaints, and access measures between the 2025 and 2026 Star Ratings?
reference_answer: For the 2026 Star Ratings "the weight of the patient experience, complaints, and access measures was decreased from 4 to 2"; in the 2025 Star Ratings those measures sat just below the improvement measures in weighting priority, ahead of outcome and intermediate outcome measures.
